blocks.text: 1 Samuel 18 contains 30 verses. It opens with: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul. It concludes with: Then the princes of the Philistines went forth: and it came to pass, as often as they went forth, that David behaved himself more wisely than all the servants of Saul; so that his name was much set by. Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: The book explicitly attributes a harmful spirit affecting Saul to the LORD after the Spirit of the LORD departs; medical, psychological, spiritual, and theological explanations should not be collapsed into one diagnosis.
